title: Artifactory Vulnerabilities Under Active Exploitation Enable Authentication Bypass and Admin Access
gist: Wiz disclosed three actively exploited Artifactory vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-42018, CVE-2026-42016, CVE-2026-82329) that let attackers take persistent admin control of internet-exposed self-hosted instances in under five minutes, posing a direct software supply-chain risk with lagging patch adoption.

insights.claim: Three Artifactory vulnerabilities under active exploitation enable authentication bypass on internet-accessible self-hosted deployments, potentially giving attackers persistent administrator access in under five minutes.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Immediate incident risk for enterprises self-hosting Artifactory; reputational and remediation cost exposure.
insights.locator: Three Artifactory vulnerabilities under active exploitation

insights.claim: Wiz.io says the CVEs are trivial to exploit with a handful of unauthenticated HTTP requests, and exposed instances should assume compromise because upgrading does not evict attackers already inside.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Patching alone is insufficient; incident response and forensics demand will rise.
insights.quote: These CVEs are trivial to exploit, a handful of unauthenticated HTTP requests.

insights.claim: Attackers chain CVE-2026-42018, which returns an internal anonymous-user JWT to unauthenticated requests, with CVE-2026-42016's scope-validation flaw to exchange it for an admin-scoped token that still appears as token:anonymous.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Escalated tokens masquerade as anonymous, complicating detection.
insights.locator: Every exploitation followed a similar shape.

insights.claim: CVE-2026-82329, rated critical, allows an unauthenticated attacker to obtain an admin-scoped token directly.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: A single critical flaw grants full control, raising severity of exposure.

insights.claim: After gaining admin access, attackers created persistent admin accounts, deployed malicious Groovy plugins for code execution, harvested credentials and Access signing keys, established backdoors and deployed anti-forensics.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Theft of signing keys enables downstream supply-chain tampering.

insights.claim: Because Artifactory sits at the center of many software supply chains, Erik York warned this kind of bug could become next year's SolarWinds story if not patched quickly.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Potential for a large-scale supply-chain incident with broad market and regulatory impact.
insights.quote: This is exactly the kind of bug that turns into next year's SolarWinds story if it's not patched fast.
insights.locator: Commenting on the disclosure on LinkedIn

insights.claim: Graylog's Jim Nitterauer said patch adoption has lagged badly, with attacks observed within four days of disclosure of the third bug.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Short exploit windows and slow patching amplify enterprise exposure.
insights.quote: patch adoption has lagged badly, with attacks observed within four days of disclosure of the third bug

insights.claim: Self-hosted Artifactory should be patched immediately to fixed versions including 7.111.21, 7.117.28, 7.125.20, 7.133.29, 7.146.38, 7.161.20 or newer depending on release branch.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Wide spread of affected branches implies a large installed base needing remediation.
